ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, EF is the perpendicular bisector of AB, intersecting AB at point D. If BF = 6 and CF = 2, then what is the length of AC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since EF is the perpendicular bisector of AB, and BF = 6, \\
we have AF=BF=6, \\
and since CF = 2, \\
it follows that AC=AF+CF=\boxed{8}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is △ABC, A is above, B is at the lower right, and C is lower and slightly to the left; point F is located on side AC, and is between C and A on segment AC. Line EF starts from point E on the left side, passes through F, and continues to reach point D on AB, so F is on EF, and D is on AB. Reasoning: The problem gives that EF is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Any point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the two endpoints A and B of the segment. Because F is on EF, AF = BF. It is known that BF = 6, therefore AF = 6. Also because in the figure C, F, A are collinear and F is between C and A, and it is known that CF = 2, so AC = CF + FA = 2 + 6 = 8.
